title: Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters
subtitle: Nintendo / Tose · Game Boy

body: Kid Icarus: Of Myths and Monsters is Nintendo and Tose's Game Boy action platformer about Pit recovering three sacred treasures to defend Angel Land. Palutena sends the young angel through training and dangerous fortresses after foreseeing an invasion by Orcos. The bow supplies his regular attack, while shops, chambers and hidden passages interrupt the climb through the surrounding worlds. The handheld sequel keeps the earlier game's mixture of combat and exploration, giving Pit a journey whose useful discoveries can be as important as reaching the next platform safely.

The stages scroll in all four directions, allowing Pit to return through places already crossed. Flapping his wings slows a fall, giving the player another way to adjust a difficult landing. Hidden doors lead to shops, hints, healing and training, with hearts collected from monsters used as currency. The route therefore contains reasons to stop and investigate instead of continually moving upward. A room reached through careful exploration may provide the strength or equipment that makes the next dangerous stretch more manageable.

Successful training can grant additional weapons, while the fortresses protect the treasures needed for the final confrontation. The game arrived in North America in 1991 and Europe in 1992, but its first Japanese release came through the Nintendo 3DS Virtual Console in 2012. That unusual publication history left this chapter less familiar in the series' home country for many years. Its character remains recognisably Kid Icarus: an angel with a bow gradually earns the means to complete a journey through a world of mythological dangers and peculiar helpful rooms.
story_headings: Look back through a more forgiving world
A Nintendo adventure first released overseas
